paper_metadata.title: Generative quantum learning of joint probability distribution functions

summary: The paper demonstrates quantum generative modeling of a two-variable financial dataset (AAPL/MSFT daily returns) using QGAN and QCBM circuits with up to 6 qubits (QGAN) and 8 qubits (QCBM) on IonQ trapped-ion hardware. The QGAN achieved DKS ≈ 0.0352 with p-value ≈ 0.357 on hardware, comparable to classical GAN and Gaussian copula baselines. Training required ~1000 iterations and up to two weeks of cloud QPU runtime for the QGAN experiment.

experiments.description: QGAN-based generative learning of the joint distribution of AAPL and MSFT daily returns in copula space, trained on simulator and IonQ trapped-ion hardware.

algorithm.variant: quantum generative adversarial network (QGAN) with qopula ansatz
algorithm.ansatz: qopula circuit: Bell-pair entangling layer followed by local single-qubit RZ/RX rotations and RXX entanglers
algorithm.optimizer: SPSA for quantum generator; stochastic gradient descent with adaptive optimizer (e.g., Adam) for classical discriminator (exact optimizer not explicitly specified)
algorithm.parameter_initialization: random initialization with same seed for simulator and experiment; parameters uniformly random from [0, 2π] for simulator runs

problem_formulation.encoding_details: daily returns transformed to copula space via probability integral transform; 3 qubits per variable used to represent discretized copula samples, with additional 40 random bits appended after measurement to reduce discretization artifacts
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize binary cross-entropy loss between generated and real samples in copula space via adversarial training
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: uniform marginals enforced by copula transform; no explicit penalty terms

problem_instance.description: Learning the joint distribution of two stock returns (AAPL and MSFT) from historical market data

dataset_specification.description: AAPL and MSFT close-price daily returns from 2010–2018; transformed to copula space

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: daily returns computed as percentage change of close prices; probability integral transform applied to map to uniform marginals; synthetic samples mapped back to original space via inverse transform
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: 2D Kolmogorov–Smirnov test comparing generated samples with bootstrapped training data; 2048 samples used for QGAN and classical GAN; p-values and DKS reported in Table I

noise_model.noise_type: depolarizing noise up to 4% after each two-qubit gate; hardware noise on IonQ cloud QPU
noise_model.mitigation_details: comparison against mixed-state noisy simulator; no explicit mitigation

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: copula transform of returns; random bits appended to measurement outputs
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: inverse probability integral transform back to return space; 2D KS test evaluation
implementation_details.total_execution_time: approximately 2 weeks for QGAN experiment on cloud QPU

convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: generator and discriminator losses diverge then converge; stable after convergence

speedup_claims.conditions: reported for the QGAN training on the AAPL/MSFT copula task; compared against equivalent classical models
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states this as an observed result; exact iteration counts for the classical GAN convergence on the same benchmark are not fully detailed beyond 20000 training iterations in the comparison discussion.

speedup_claims.conditions: IonQ cloud QPU and noisy simulator with up to 4% depolarizing noise after each two-qubit gate
speedup_claims.caveats: This is qualitative rather than a numeric speedup.

speedup_claims.factor: potential exponential advantage for some joint distributions
speedup_claims.conditions: for qopula circuits under complexity-theoretic assumptions (PH does not collapse to level 3)
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a complexity-theoretic argument, not a benchmark-specific demonstrated speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: claimed advantage from shallow circuits; no explicit asymptotic runtime for QGAN training
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: not explicitly quantified for QGAN training; classical GAN training reported as 20000 iterations in comparison
complexity_analysis.wall_clock_classical: about 6 minutes for classical GAN on CPU-only machine

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not established; authors speculate usefulness around ~50 qubits for practical datasets
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Authors estimate ~5–10 qubits per variable and ~10–100 variables (≈50+ qubits total) may enable practical applications
limiting_factors: Generative task evaluated on a 2-variable dataset
Classical GAN and Gaussian copula perform similarly
Quantum runtime extremely slow (≈2 weeks via cloud access)
No asymptotic speedup demonstrated for the practical learning task

notes: circuit_depth not explicitly stated for QGAN; one ansatz layer is reported, but total depth is not given.
hardware.type reported from IonQ cloud QPU experiments.
speedup_order set to none_proven because the paper argues advantage but does not provide a fully established asymptotic speedup for the specific QGAN experiment.
Authors claim theoretical computational advantage based on IQP-style arguments and communication complexity.
However, the experimental results only show comparable performance to classical baselines on a very small dataset.

experiments.description: QCBM-based generative learning of the same AAPL/MSFT copula distribution, evaluated on simulator, IonQ cloud QPU, and IonQ next-generation QPU across 2, 4, 6, and 8 qubits.

algorithm.variant: quantum circuit born machine (QCBM) with qopula-inspired ansatz
algorithm.ansatz: one-layer qopula ansatz with local RZ/RX rotations and RXX entanglers; Bell/GHZ-style entangling initialization
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 200 iterations for experiments; minimum cost often found within 20 iterations for a=c=0.5
algorithm.parameter_initialization: initialized with optimal angles from previous smaller system size (transfer learning)

optimizer_settings.learning_rate_schedule: not explicitly stated beyond SPSA schedule

problem_formulation.encoding_details: copula-space samples discretized into 2^(Nq/2) bins; measured bitstrings mapped back to [0,1] via linear transform and random-bit padding
problem_formulation.objective_function: minimize KL divergence between target discrete copula distribution p and circuit output distribution q
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: uniform marginals enforced by copula transform; clipped KL with pi,j floored at 1e-6

problem_instance.description: Learning the joint distribution of AAPL and MSFT daily returns in copula space using a Born machine

dataset_specification.description: same AAPL/MSFT dataset as QGAN; evaluated for 2, 4, 6, and 8 qubits

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: probability integral transform to copula space; binning into 2^(Nq/2) bins; inverse transform for visualization
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: training on simulator, IonQ cloud QPU, and IonQ next-generation QPU; average of 10 minimum cost values; 2D KS test and DKS/p-values reported

hardware.device_name: IonQ cloud QPU; IonQ next-generation QPU

noise_model.noise_type: hardware noise on trapped-ion QPUs; noisy behavior discussed qualitatively
noise_model.mitigation_details: no explicit mitigation; noisy hardware sometimes improved early optimization
noise_model.classical_postprocessing: random-bit padding and inverse transform for visualization
noise_model.total_execution_time: approximately 5 hours on next-generation QPU; about 9 hours on cloud system for 6-qubit case

convergence_data.iterations_to_converge: within 20 iterations for a=c=0.5; slower convergence shown for a=c=0.1
convergence_data.loss_curve_shape: cost decreases with iterations; noisier for larger qubit counts

implementation_details.total_execution_time: approximately 5 hours for 6-qubit training on next-generation QPU and approximately 9 hours on IonQ cloud system (200 iterations)

speedup_claims.conditions: QCBM training on AAPL/MSFT copula data; minimum cost often found within 20 iterations for a=c=0.5
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper does not provide a single exact classical iteration count for the same QCBM objective; the comparison is qualitative and based on the reported 20000 classical GAN iterations in the broader discussion.

speedup_claims.factor: potential exponential advantage for some distributions
speedup_claims.conditions: complexity-theoretic arguments for qopula circuits and related shallow-circuit separations
speedup_claims.caveats: This is not a benchmark-specific measured speedup.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: no explicit asymptotic runtime; paper argues shallow-circuit advantage and better scaling than classical for some distributions
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: not explicitly quantified for QCBM; classical comparison via GAN and parametric Gaussian copula

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Likely requires tens of qubits per variable and larger datasets to test expressivity advantages

No scaling comparison against classical generative models at larger dimension
Advantage arguments rely on worst-case circuit complexity rather than demonstrated learning performance
